answer: Attention-Debt Scheduling. Each identity must complete a randomized daily sequence of small cognitive tasks whose order depends on a private seed, so operating many identities forces parallel, sustained attention rather than precomputed answers. A vine of task history records timing variance; a grove of scheduled slots constrains how many identities one operator can genuinely service per hour. Any account whose completion pattern acts as a mirror of another's timing gets throttled. An attacker pays hours of real attentiveness per identity per day, capping farm width.
